## Where we've been

- Under **i.i.d random sampling** from the target population, we've established that...

<!-- Each row keeps its left-hand side fixed while the right-hand side steps
     through the week 6 derivation in place (fade-in-then-out fragments in an
     r-stack), with the assumption used at each step noted underneath. The
     last step stays up. Layout in custom.scss (.recap-row). -->
::: {.recap-row}

$\mathbb{E}[\hat{\mu}] =$

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="1"}
$\displaystyle \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right]$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="2"}
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}[Y_i]$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="3"}
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \mu$
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}
$\displaystyle \mu$
:::
:::

::: {.r-stack .recap-note}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="2"}
linearity of expectations
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="3"}
**identical**: $\mathbb{E}[Y_i] = \mu$
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}
unbiased
:::
:::

:::

::: {.recap-row}

$\Var(\hat{\mu}) =$

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="5"}
$\displaystyle \Var\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right)$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="6"}
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{n^2}\left[\sum_{i=1}^n \Var(Y_i) + \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j \neq i} \Cov(Y_i, Y_j)\right]$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="7"}
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \Var(Y_i)$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="8"}
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma^2$
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index="9"}
$\displaystyle \frac{\sigma^2}{n}$
:::
:::

::: {.r-stack .recap-note}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="6"}
constants out squared; variance of a sum
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="7"}
**independent**: $\Cov(Y_i, Y_j) = 0$
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index="8"}
**identical**: $\Var(Y_i) = \sigma^2$
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index="9"}
sampling variance
:::
:::

:::

::: {.fragment .recap-result fragment-index="10"}
$\hat{\mu} \sim \; {\color{#c5050c}{?}}\left(\mu, \dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$
:::

## This week

::: {.incremental}

- **Convergence in distribution**
  - As sample size $n$ becomes large, is the sampling distribution **well-approximated** by a known distribution?
  - When a **central limit theorem** applies, the sampling distribution **converges in distribution** to a normal!

- **Plug-in estimation**
  - What if we want to learn other things about the **population** distribution?
  - A population *variance*? A population *covariance*?
  - Like the mean, these are all **functionals** of the population CDF
  - Under i.i.d. sampling, plugging in the **sample** CDF usually gives a good estimator!

- **Density estimation**
  - Histograms and binning
  - **Kernel** estimators (weighted averages w/ weights determined by *closeness*)

:::
